draft.title: The Fair Work system
card: The Fair Work Act 2009 is the national law that sets the rules for most workplaces in Australia. It covers matters such as pay, conditions, termination of employment and bargaining.
the national workplace tribunal. It sets minimum wages, makes and varies modern awards, approves enterprise agreements and settles disputes, such as unfair dismissal claims.
the agency that enforces the law. It gives advice, investigates complaints about underpayment and can take legal action against employers who break the rules.
The two bodies have different jobs. One makes decisions and sets rules, such as wage rates. The other checks that employers follow the law and acts when they do not.
draft.remember: The Act sets the rules. The Commission decides, sets wages and makes awards. The Ombudsman enforces.

a.q: Which national body sets minimum wages and makes modern awards for workplaces across Australia?
opts: A single employer's human resources team
a.why: The Fair Work Commission is the tribunal that sets minimum wages and makes and varies modern awards. The Fair Work Ombudsman is tempting, but its job is to enforce the law and investigate breaches, not to set wage rates.
a.clue: Which body makes decisions and sets rules, rather than enforcing them?

b.q: Mia works at a bakery in Geelong and learns she has been underpaid for months. She wants the underpayment investigated and, if needed, taken to court. Which body should she contact?
b.why: The Fair Work Ombudsman enforces the law. It investigates underpayment complaints and can take legal action. The Fair Work Commission is tempting, but it sets wages, makes awards and settles disputes. It does not investigate and prosecute breaches.
b.clue: Which body checks that employers follow the law and acts when they do not?
